- Long-report generation (LLMs with 60k token context, peak concurrency ~6)

Hi Priya / Tom —

Really helpful context, thanks. I sketched an initial hedge/tiling plan and attached a spreadsheet (sku_tradeoffs_v1.xlsx) that walks through three scenarios (memory-first, throughput-first, and mixed). High-level recommendations up-front:

- Memory-first tier: H100 (80 GB) for the long-report models — this minimizes OOMs and reduces expensive tiling overhead for 60k contexts. Expect ~40–60% lower token-generation latency for very long contexts vs A100 in our tests.
- Balanced tier: A100 (40 GB) as the backbone for most conversational workloads and mid-length generation. Good tokens/sec per dollar for steady-state.
- Economy/burst tier: L4 (24 GB) for embeddings, short prompts, and background batch jobs; much cheaper per-hour — good for spiky, high-concurrency embedding traffic.

I asked ops to validate the mix that hits your $65k target given your concurrency profile — looping them in now. Can you confirm (a) expected sustained qps per pool and (b) any regulatory constraints for private networking or HSM?

Next steps: ops will validate autoscale headroom and fallback routing. If you can share a slightly larger trace (24h), we can simulate cost under different utilization assumptions.

Thanks,

Rafael / team — quick ops breakdown based on the sample payload:

Assumptions from traces:
- Long-report jobs: average 40k tokens generated (peak up to 60k), concurrency 4–8, average request duration 60–180s.
- Embeddings/short prompts: avg 256 tokens, burst concurrency up to 120, typical latency requirement < 150ms p95.

SKU characteristics (approx.):
- H100 (80 GB GPU memory): best for very long context; peak tokens/sec for long sequences ~ 1.2–1.8k tokens/sec per GPU depending on model family and quantization. Memory headroom avoids tiling. Cost (committed-equivalent) — assume $35–45/hr equivalent.
- A100 (40 GB): solid middle ground; tokens/sec ~ 2.5–4k for short-to-mid contexts, but long-context throughput degrades due to KV sharding and spill/tiling overhead. Cost ~ $12–18/hr equivalent.
- L4 (24 GB): optimized for short prompts and embedding; tokens/sec high for short contexts (embeddings throughput very good when batched), cost ~ $2–5/hr equivalent.

Recommendation (initial committed pool to match $65k target):
- Reserve 4 H100 nodes for the memory tier (handles long-report concurrency, gives headroom for 6 concurrent long jobs with some batching).
- Reserve 10 A100 nodes for the balanced tier (handles steady conversational traffic + mid-length generation).
- Reserve 6 L4 nodes for bursty embeddings and low-cost fallbacks.

Rationale: this mix gives you a memory-first safety net (H100) while keeping most steady traffic on A100 where cost-efficiency is higher. L4 absorbs most short-request bursts and background batch jobs.

Fallbacks & routing:
- Primary routing: classify by model/profile — if job requires >40k context or marked as "long-report", route to H100.
- Overflow policy: if memory tier is saturated, we can queue or tile onto A100 with aggressive KV checkpointing but with higher latency; only if the customer accepts degraded p95.
- For embeddings bursts, autoscale L4 pool and apply aggressive batching (prefetch + prefix cache) to keep p95 under 150ms.

Ops notes:
- Enable persistent KV cache for long-report models on H100 to avoid repeated recomputation.
- Provide canary autoscale: start with conservative concurrency limits for H100 (to ensure tail latency), increase after 2-week telemetry window.

I'll run a cost sim against a synthetic 24h trace if Priya shares it. We should also include an L4 prewarm policy to handle spikes.
